title: SimpleDateFormat is NOT thread-safe — mutable Calendar state, ThreadLocal fix, DateTimeFormatter best
shortTitle: SimpleDateFormat is NOT thread-safe — mutable Calendar state, ThreadLocal fix, DateTimeFormatter best

s1_definition.profdef: `SimpleDateFormat` is NOT thread-safe because it holds a mutable `Calendar` field internally. When `format()` or `parse()` is called, it writes to this Calendar. Two threads calling `format()` simultaneously on the SAME SimpleDateFormat instance corrupt each other's Calendar → garbled dates, wrong dates, or `NumberFormatException`. Three fixes: (1) **New instance per call** — safe but slow (object creation overhead). (2) **ThreadLocal<SimpleDateFormat>** — one instance per thread, no sharing, no corruption. (3) **`DateTimeFormatter` (Java 8+)** — BEST. Immutable, thread-safe by design, no ThreadLocal needed. A single static final instance shared safely by all threads.
s1_definition.analogy: `SimpleDateFormat` is like a SHARED CALCULATOR on a desk. Teller-1 types "25/10/2024" → calculator shows intermediate result. Teller-2 types "15/03/2025" SIMULTANEOUSLY on the SAME calculator → both results garbled! "35/13/2025"! **ThreadLocal** = each teller gets their OWN calculator. No sharing. **DateTimeFormatter** = a READ-ONLY printed conversion chart on the wall. 100 tellers read it simultaneously → no corruption. Nobody writes on it — it's immutable.
s1_definition.oneliner: SimpleDateFormat: mutable Calendar → not thread-safe. ThreadLocal: one per thread (fix). DateTimeFormatter: immutable → thread-safe by design (best). Always use java.time in new code.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** `SimpleDateFormat` is NOT thread-safe because it holds a mutable `Calendar` field internally. When `format()` or `parse()` is called, it writes to this Calendar. Two threads calling `format()` simultaneously on the SAME SimpleDateFormat instance corrupt each other's Calendar → garbled dates, wrong dates, or `NumberFormatException`. Three fixes: (1) **New instance per call** — safe but slow (object creation overhead). (2) **ThreadLocal<SimpleDateFormat>** — one instance per thread, no sharing, no corruption. (3) **`DateTimeFormatter` (Java 8+)** — BEST. Immutable, thread-safe by design, no ThreadLocal needed. A single static final instance shared safely by all threads.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** `SimpleDateFormat` is like a SHARED CALCULATOR on a desk. Teller-1 types "25/10/2024" → calculator shows intermediate result. Teller-2 types "15/03/2025" SIMULTANEOUSLY on the SAME calculator → both results garbled! "35/13/2025"! **ThreadLocal** = each teller gets their OWN calculator. No sharing. **DateTimeFormatter** = a READ-ONLY printed conversion chart on the wall. 100 tellers read it simultaneously → no corruption. Nobody writes on it — it's immutable.

**One line to remember:** SimpleDateFormat: mutable Calendar → not thread-safe. ThreadLocal: one per thread (fix). DateTimeFormatter: immutable → thread-safe by design (best). Always use java.time in new code.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The trade confirmation service used a static `SimpleDateFormat` to format settlement dates.** Under load (200 concurrent threads), the formatted dates were garbled: "2024-13-45" instead of "2024-10-18", some trades showed dates from other trades, and occasional `NumberFormatException` crashed the formatter. 50 trade confirmations per day had wrong dates. Customers received confirmations with dates from OTHER customers' trades. Fix: replaced `SimpleDateFormat` with `DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("yyyy-MM-dd")` — one static final instance, zero bugs, zero ThreadLocal overhead.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1 (Bug).** 50 threads share ONE SimpleDateFormat. Thread-1 calls `sdf.format(date1)` → writes date1 to internal Calendar. Thread-2 calls `sdf.format(date2)` → OVERWRITES the Calendar with date2. Thread-1 reads from Calendar → gets mixed data → "2024-13-45".

**Step 2 (ThreadLocal fix).** Each thread gets its own SimpleDateFormat via `ThreadLocal.withInitial()`. Thread-1 formats on its own SDF. Thread-2 formats on its own SDF. No sharing → no corruption. Must call `remove()` in thread pools!

**Step 3 (DateTimeFormatter fix).** ONE static final instance. 50 threads call `LocalDate.now().format(DTF)` simultaneously. DTF is immutable — no internal state mutation. Every call is independent. Zero bugs. Zero ThreadLocal. Zero remove() needed.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ SimpleDateFormat: MUTABLE → NOT thread-safe ═══

  Thread-1: sdf.format(date1) → calendar.setTime(date1) → read calendar
  Thread-2: sdf.format(date2) → calendar.setTime(date2) → OVERWRITES!
  Thread-1 reads: GARBLED! date1 fields mixed with date2 fields!

  ═══ DateTimeFormatter: IMMUTABLE → thread-safe ═══

  Thread-1: localDate.format(DTF) → creates new String → no shared state!
  Thread-2: localDate.format(DTF) → creates new String → independent!
  DTF has ZERO mutable fields → impossible to corrupt!

  ═══ MIGRATION ═══
  SimpleDateFormat → DateTimeFormatter
  Date            → LocalDate / LocalDateTime
  Calendar        → LocalDate (immutable!)
  ThreadLocal<SDF> → static final DateTimeFormatter (simpler!)
```

sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — SimpleDateFormat vs DateTimeFormatter ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
  │  SimpleDateFormat                 │
  │  - calendar: Calendar (MUTABLE!) │ ← shared, mutated on every format/parse!
  │  - pattern: String               │
  │  + format(Date): String          │ writes to calendar!
  │  + parse(String): Date           │ writes to calendar!
  │  Thread-safe: NO ❌              │
  └──────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
  │  DateTimeFormatter                │
  │  - all fields: FINAL (immutable!)│ ← no mutable state!
  │  + format(TemporalAccessor): String│ creates new String, no side effects!
  │  + parse(String): TemporalAccessor │ no side effects!
  │  Thread-safe: YES ✅              │
  │  Singleton: static final OK!      │
  └──────────────────────────────────┘

  Decision:
  Legacy code (pre-Java 8): ThreadLocal<SimpleDateFormat>
  New code (Java 8+):       static final DateTimeFormatter (always!)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
SimpleDateFormat is NOT thread-safe because it holds a mutable Calendar field internally. `format()` and `parse()` write to this Calendar — two threads sharing one instance corrupt each other's data, producing garbled dates, wrong dates, or NumberFormatException. This is one of the most common Java concurrency bugs in production.

Three fixes: (1) Create a new instance per call — safe but slow. (2) `ThreadLocal<SimpleDateFormat>` — one per thread, must call `remove()` in pools. (3) `DateTimeFormatter` (Java 8+) — BEST. Immutable, thread-safe by design. ONE static final instance shared by all threads. No ThreadLocal, no remove(), no bugs. Always use `java.time` (LocalDate, LocalDateTime, DateTimeFormatter) in new code. In banking: trade confirmation service with 200 threads — static SimpleDateFormat garbled 50 dates/day. Replaced with `static final DateTimeFormatter` — zero bugs, zero overhead.
